# Purpose

This notebook creates a joint respondent-level bootstrap sensitivity for the
eight AMIS inputs used by the dynamic pathway model. It does **not** rerake the
survey in every replicate. Instead, it:

1. starts from the existing cleaned data and final calibrated (`raked_weight`)
   weights;
2. resamples complete respondent records with replacement within each
   state-by-period cell;
3. carries the same resampled respondent, weight, observed outcomes, and
   missingness pattern through all eight measures;
4. calculates state, Census-division, and national estimates from the same
   replicate;
5. applies the same survey-year exclusions and variable definitions used to
   construct the `trends` sheet of `Factor Analysis v5.xlsx`; and
6. uses the resulting bootstrap estimates directly as the model-input draws.

Because the complete production estimator is reproduced, no recentering or
logit-shift step is used. The final raking weights are held fixed rather than
re-estimated within each replicate.

The default is a 100-replicate diagnostic. Increase `n_boot` to 500 only after
the marginal uncertainty, joint correlations, and downstream pilot fits have
been reviewed.

# Setup

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE,
  message = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE,
  fig.width = 10,
  fig.height = 6
)

required_packages <- c(
  "dplyr", "tidyr", "purrr", "readr", "readxl", "ggplot2", "tibble"
)
missing_packages <- required_packages[
  !vapply(required_packages, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE)
]
if (length(missing_packages) > 0) {
  stop(
    "Install the following R packages before rendering: ",
    paste(missing_packages, collapse = ", ")
  )
}

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)
library(readr)
library(readxl)
library(ggplot2)
library(tibble)

set.seed(params$seed)
dir.create(params$output_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

model_variables <- c(
  "stigma_ahs",
  "stigma_gss",
  "stigma_family",
  "out_gid",
  "seehcp",
  "risk_behavior",
  "prep_used",
  "hivtest12"
)

model_periods <- c(
  "2017-2018" = 2018L,
  "2019-2020" = 2020L,
  "2021-2022" = 2022L,
  "2023-2024" = 2024L
)

logit_safe <- function(x, eps = params$eps) {
  x <- pmin(pmax(as.numeric(x), eps), 1 - eps)
  qlogis(x)
}

inv_logit_safe <- function(x, eps = params$eps) {
  pmin(pmax(plogis(as.numeric(x)), eps), 1 - eps)
}

weighted_mean_safe <- function(x, w) {
  keep <- is.finite(x) & is.finite(w) & w > 0
  if (!any(keep)) return(NA_real_)
  sum(x[keep] * w[keep]) / sum(w[keep])
}

kish_neff_safe <- function(w) {
  keep <- is.finite(w) & w > 0
  if (!any(keep)) return(NA_real_)
  denom <- sum(w[keep]^2)
  if (!is.finite(denom) || denom <= 0) return(NA_real_)
  sum(w[keep])^2 / denom
}
```

# Load and validate the final weighted respondent data

```{r load-data}
if (!file.exists(params$input_rds)) {
  stop("Input RDS not found: ", params$input_rds)
}
if (!file.exists(params$factor_workbook)) {
  stop("Factor-analysis workbook not found: ", params$factor_workbook)
}
if (!file.exists(params$msm_population_path)) {
  stop("MSM population file not found: ", params$msm_population_path)
}

amis_svy_df <- readRDS(params$input_rds)
if (is.list(amis_svy_df) && "variables" %in% names(amis_svy_df)) {
  amis_df <- amis_svy_df$variables
} else if (is.data.frame(amis_svy_df)) {
  amis_df <- amis_svy_df
} else {
  stop("The input RDS must be a data frame or contain a $variables data frame.")
}

required_columns <- c(
  "rowID", "state_calc", "_censdiv", "year_group", "raked_weight",
  "survey", "_hivstat",
  model_variables
)
missing_columns <- setdiff(required_columns, names(amis_df))
if (length(missing_columns) > 0) {
  stop("Weighted respondent data are missing: ", paste(missing_columns, collapse = ", "))
}

# Reproduce the HIV-testing definition used in EEE AMIS Bayesian Sampling v4.
if ("test2yrs" %in% names(amis_df)) {
  amis_df <- amis_df %>%
    mutate(
      hivtest12_original = hivtest12,
      test2yrs_raw = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(as.character(test2yrs))),
      test2yrs_num = if_else(
        test2yrs_raw >= 0 & test2yrs_raw <= 100,
        test2yrs_raw,
        NA_real_
      ),
      hivtest12 = pmin(test2yrs_num, 4) / 4
    )
}

amis_analysis <- amis_df %>%
  filter(
    `_hivstat` != 2,
    !survey %in% c("amis_15", "amis_16")
  ) %>%
  transmute(
    rowID = as.character(rowID),
    state_calc = as.character(state_calc),
    census_division = suppressWarnings(as.integer(as.character(`_censdiv`))),
    year_group = as.character(year_group),
    raked_weight = as.numeric(raked_weight),
    across(all_of(model_variables), ~ suppressWarnings(as.numeric(as.character(.x))))
  ) %>%
  filter(
    year_group %in% names(model_periods),
    !is.na(state_calc),
    !is.na(census_division),
    !is.na(raked_weight),
    is.finite(raked_weight),
    raked_weight > 0
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    year = unname(model_periods[year_group]),
    stratum = interaction(state_calc, year_group, drop = TRUE, lex.order = TRUE)
  )

if (anyDuplicated(amis_analysis$rowID)) {
  # rowID need not be globally unique across annual source files. The combination
  # below is used only for auditing; bootstrap sampling uses row positions.
  amis_analysis <- amis_analysis %>%
    mutate(respondent_key = paste(state_calc, year_group, rowID, sep = "::"))
} else {
  amis_analysis <- amis_analysis %>% mutate(respondent_key = rowID)
}

stopifnot(length(unique(amis_analysis$year_group)) == length(model_periods))
stopifnot(all(model_variables %in% names(amis_analysis)))

data_inventory <- amis_analysis %>%
  group_by(state_calc, census_division, year_group, year) %>%
  summarise(
    n_respondents = n(),
    weight_min = min(raked_weight),
    weight_median = median(raked_weight),
    weight_max = max(raked_weight),
    weight_cv = sd(raked_weight) / mean(raked_weight),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

data_inventory
```

# Load the model's central trajectories and state aggregation weights

```{r load-model-centers}
factor_trends <- read_excel(params$factor_workbook, sheet = "trends") %>%
  transmute(
    unit = as.character(Geography),
    year = as.integer(Year),
    variable = as.character(Indicator),
    model_center = as.numeric(Value)
  ) %>%
  filter(year %in% unname(model_periods), variable %in% model_variables) %>%
  mutate(model_center = pmin(pmax(model_center, params$eps), 1 - params$eps))

state_metadata <- read_excel(params$factor_workbook, sheet = "states") %>%
  transmute(
    state_calc = as.character(state_calc),
    state_model_n = as.numeric(n),
    census_division = as.integer(Census_div)
  )

state_msm_population <- read_csv(params$msm_population_path, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  transmute(
    state_calc = as.character(state),
    state_msm_pop = as.numeric(rounded)
  )

state_metadata <- state_metadata %>%
  left_join(state_msm_population, by = "state_calc")

if (any(is.na(state_metadata$state_msm_pop))) {
  stop("MSM population weights are missing for one or more modeled states.")
}

if (anyDuplicated(factor_trends[c("unit", "year", "variable")])) {
  stop("The factor-analysis trends sheet has duplicate unit-year-variable rows.")
}

state_centers <- factor_trends %>%
  filter(unit != "USA") %>%
  inner_join(state_metadata, by = c("unit" = "state_calc"))

division_centers <- state_centers %>%
  group_by(census_division, year, variable) %>%
  summarise(
    model_center = weighted_mean_safe(model_center, state_model_n),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(unit = paste0("div_", census_division)) %>%
  select(unit, year, variable, model_center)

model_centers <- bind_rows(
  factor_trends %>% select(unit, year, variable, model_center),
  division_centers
) %>%
  distinct(unit, year, variable, .keep_all = TRUE)

model_center_coverage <- model_centers %>%
  count(unit, name = "n_model_cells") %>%
  arrange(unit)

model_center_coverage
```

# Weighted-estimate functions

```{r functions}
summarize_weighted_cells <- function(data, group_columns, unit_expression) {
  long <- data %>%
    select(all_of(group_columns), raked_weight, all_of(model_variables)) %>%
    pivot_longer(
      cols = all_of(model_variables),
      names_to = "variable",
      values_to = "response"
    ) %>%
    filter(!is.na(response), is.finite(response)) %>%
    group_by(across(all_of(c(group_columns, "variable")))) %>%
    summarise(
      weighted_prop = weighted_mean_safe(response, raked_weight),
      n_eff = kish_neff_safe(raked_weight),
      n_obs = n(),
      sum_weights = sum(raked_weight),
      .groups = "drop"
    )

  long %>% mutate(unit = {{ unit_expression }})
}

summarize_all_geographies <- function(data) {
  state <- summarize_weighted_cells(
    data,
    c("state_calc", "year_group", "year"),
    state_calc
  ) %>%
    mutate(geography_type = "state")

  division_direct <- summarize_weighted_cells(
    data,
    c("census_division", "year_group", "year"),
    paste0("div_", census_division)
  ) %>%
    mutate(geography_type = "division_direct")

  usa <- summarize_weighted_cells(
    data %>% mutate(usa = "USA"),
    c("usa", "year_group", "year"),
    usa
  ) %>%
    mutate(geography_type = "nation")

  bind_rows(
    state %>% select(unit, geography_type, year_group, year, variable,
                     weighted_prop, n_eff, n_obs, sum_weights),
    division_direct %>% select(unit, geography_type, year_group, year, variable,
                               weighted_prop, n_eff, n_obs, sum_weights),
    usa %>% select(unit, geography_type, year_group, year, variable,
                   weighted_prop, n_eff, n_obs, sum_weights)
  )
}

build_model_divisions <- function(state_summary) {
  state_summary %>%
    filter(geography_type == "state") %>%
    mutate(weighted_prop = pmin(pmax(weighted_prop, params$eps), 1 - params$eps)) %>%
    inner_join(state_metadata, by = c("unit" = "state_calc")) %>%
    group_by(census_division, year_group, year, variable) %>%
    summarise(
      weighted_prop = weighted_mean_safe(weighted_prop, state_model_n),
      n_eff = NA_real_,
      n_obs = sum(n_obs),
      sum_weights = sum(sum_weights),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      unit = paste0("div_", census_division),
      geography_type = "division_model"
    ) %>%
    select(unit, geography_type, year_group, year, variable,
           weighted_prop, n_eff, n_obs, sum_weights)
}

build_model_nation <- function(state_summary) {
  state_summary %>%
    filter(geography_type == "state") %>%
    inner_join(state_metadata, by = c("unit" = "state_calc")) %>%
    group_by(year_group, year, variable) %>%
    summarise(
      weighted_prop = weighted_mean_safe(weighted_prop, state_msm_pop),
      n_eff = NA_real_,
      n_obs = sum(n_obs),
      sum_weights = sum(sum_weights),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    mutate(unit = "USA", geography_type = "nation_model") %>%
    select(unit, geography_type, year_group, year, variable,
           weighted_prop, n_eff, n_obs, sum_weights)
}

resample_within_state_period <- function(data) {
  split_rows <- split(seq_len(nrow(data)), data$stratum, drop = TRUE)
  sampled_rows <- unlist(
    lapply(split_rows, function(idx) sample(idx, size = length(idx), replace = TRUE)),
    use.names = FALSE
  )
  data[sampled_rows, , drop = FALSE]
}
```

# Original weighted estimates

```{r original-estimates}
original_direct <- summarize_all_geographies(amis_analysis)
original_model_divisions <- build_model_divisions(original_direct)
original_model_nation <- build_model_nation(original_direct)

original_estimates <- bind_rows(
  original_direct,
  original_model_divisions,
  original_model_nation
) %>%
  rename(original_weighted_prop = weighted_prop)

original_estimates %>%
  count(geography_type, variable, name = "n_cells")
```

# Generate respondent-bootstrap replicates

Each replicate resamples complete rows within state-period strata. State,
division, and national summaries are then calculated from the same replicate.
The final raking weights are carried with respondents and are not recalculated.

```{r bootstrap, cache=TRUE}
set.seed(params$seed)

bootstrap_list <- vector("list", params$n_boot)
for (b in seq_len(params$n_boot)) {
  sampled <- resample_within_state_period(amis_analysis)
  direct <- summarize_all_geographies(sampled)
  model_division <- build_model_divisions(direct)
  model_nation <- build_model_nation(direct)

  bootstrap_list[[b]] <- bind_rows(direct, model_division, model_nation) %>%
    mutate(draw = b, .before = 1)

  if (b %% 10 == 0 || b == params$n_boot) {
    message("Completed bootstrap replicate ", b, " of ", params$n_boot)
  }
}

bootstrap_estimates <- bind_rows(bootstrap_list) %>%
  rename(bootstrap_weighted_prop = weighted_prop)

rm(bootstrap_list)
gc()
```

# Construct production-compatible direct-bootstrap draws

The production-compatible output uses state estimates and state-weighted
division and national aggregates. Direct respondent-pooled division and
national estimates are retained only as diagnostics. The bootstrap estimates
are used directly; the factor-analysis model centers are joined solely to
verify exact reproduction of the original estimator.

```{r construct-direct-draws}
production_types <- c("state", "division_model", "nation_model")

joint_model_draws <- bootstrap_estimates %>%
  filter(geography_type %in% production_types) %>%
  left_join(
    original_estimates %>%
      filter(geography_type %in% production_types) %>%
      select(
        unit, geography_type, year_group, year, variable,
        original_weighted_prop, original_n_eff = n_eff
      ),
    by = c("unit", "geography_type", "year_group", "year", "variable")
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    model_centers,
    by = c("unit", "year", "variable")
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    bootstrap_weighted_prop = pmin(
      pmax(bootstrap_weighted_prop, params$eps),
      1 - params$eps
    ),
    original_weighted_prop = pmin(
      pmax(original_weighted_prop, params$eps),
      1 - params$eps
    ),
    delta_logit = logit_safe(bootstrap_weighted_prop) -
      logit_safe(original_weighted_prop),
    model_draw = bootstrap_weighted_prop
  )

missing_model_centers <- joint_model_draws %>% filter(is.na(model_center))
if (nrow(missing_model_centers) > 0) {
  warning(
    nrow(missing_model_centers),
    " bootstrap cells lack a matching Factor Analysis v5 model center."
  )
}

joint_model_draws <- joint_model_draws %>%
  filter(!is.na(model_center), !is.na(model_draw)) %>%
  arrange(draw, geography_type, unit, year, match(variable, model_variables))

stopifnot(all(joint_model_draws$model_draw > 0 & joint_model_draws$model_draw < 1))

production_reproduction_audit <- joint_model_draws %>%
  distinct(unit, geography_type, year_group, year, variable,
           original_weighted_prop, model_center) %>%
  mutate(
    production_difference = original_weighted_prop - model_center,
    absolute_production_difference = abs(production_difference)
  )

production_reproduction <- production_reproduction_audit %>%
  filter(!is.na(model_center))

production_reproduction_summary <- production_reproduction %>%
  group_by(geography_type) %>%
  summarise(
    n_cells = n(),
    maximum_absolute_difference = max(absolute_production_difference),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
print(production_reproduction_summary)

stopifnot(max(production_reproduction$absolute_production_difference) < 1e-10)
```

# Diagnostics

## Bootstrap centering

The mean bootstrap estimate should recover the original weighted estimate.
Separately, the original state estimates must reproduce the Factor Analysis v5
trajectory values to numerical precision.

```{r centering-diagnostic}
centering_diagnostic <- bootstrap_estimates %>%
  group_by(unit, geography_type, year_group, year, variable) %>%
  summarise(
    bootstrap_mean = mean(bootstrap_weighted_prop, na.rm = TRUE),
    bootstrap_sd = sd(bootstrap_weighted_prop, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    original_estimates %>%
      select(unit, geography_type, year_group, year, variable,
             original_weighted_prop, n_eff),
    by = c("unit", "geography_type", "year_group", "year", "variable")
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    centering_difference = bootstrap_mean - original_weighted_prop,
    absolute_centering_difference = abs(centering_difference)
  )

centering_diagnostic %>%
  summarise(
    median_absolute_difference = median(absolute_centering_difference, na.rm = TRUE),
    p95_absolute_difference = quantile(absolute_centering_difference, 0.95, na.rm = TRUE),
    maximum_absolute_difference = max(absolute_centering_difference, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
```

## Comparison with the independent-Beta marginal approximation

This comparison is descriptive. The bootstrap is intended to improve the joint
sampling structure; it is not required to produce smaller marginal standard
deviations than the Beta approximation.

```{r beta-comparison}
beta_sd <- function(p, n_eff) {
  alpha <- p * n_eff + 1
  beta <- (1 - p) * n_eff + 1
  sqrt(alpha * beta / ((alpha + beta)^2 * (alpha + beta + 1)))
}

marginal_comparison <- centering_diagnostic %>%
  filter(geography_type %in% c("state", "nation_model")) %>%
  mutate(
    beta_sd = if_else(
      is.finite(n_eff) & n_eff > 0,
      beta_sd(original_weighted_prop, n_eff),
      NA_real_
    ),
    sd_ratio_bootstrap_to_beta = bootstrap_sd / beta_sd
  )

marginal_comparison %>%
  group_by(variable) %>%
  summarise(
    median_bootstrap_sd = median(bootstrap_sd, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_beta_sd = median(beta_sd, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_sd_ratio = median(sd_ratio_bootstrap_to_beta, na.rm = TRUE),
    q25_sd_ratio = quantile(sd_ratio_bootstrap_to_beta, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
    q75_sd_ratio = quantile(sd_ratio_bootstrap_to_beta, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

## Joint cross-measure uncertainty

```{r correlation-diagnostic}
joint_delta_wide <- joint_model_draws %>%
  filter(geography_type == "state") %>%
  select(draw, unit, year, variable, delta_logit) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = variable, values_from = delta_logit)

joint_delta_correlation <- cor(
  joint_delta_wide[, model_variables],
  use = "pairwise.complete.obs"
)

round(joint_delta_correlation, 3)
```

```{r plot-sd-comparison, fig.height=6}
ggplot(
  marginal_comparison,
  aes(x = beta_sd, y = bootstrap_sd, color = variable)
) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = 2, color = "grey45") +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.55, size = 1.5) +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(
    x = "Independent-Beta standard deviation",
    y = "Respondent-bootstrap standard deviation",
    color = "Measure",
    title = "Marginal uncertainty under the two input-sampling approaches"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11)
```

    "division draws use states-sheet n; national draws use state MSM population",
    paste(model_variables, collapse = "|"),
    paste(unname(model_periods), collapse = "|")

  joint_model_draws,

write_csv(metadata, file.path(params$output_dir, "amis_joint_bootstrap_metadata_v1.csv"))
write_csv(data_inventory, file.path(params$output_dir, "amis_joint_bootstrap_inventory_v1.csv"))
write_csv(centering_diagnostic,

write_csv(production_reproduction_audit,
          file.path(params$output_dir, "amis_production_reproduction_audit_v2.csv"))
write_csv(marginal_comparison,
          file.path(params$output_dir, "amis_joint_bootstrap_beta_comparison_v1.csv"))
write_csv(
  as.data.frame(joint_delta_correlation) %>%
    rownames_to_column("variable"),

)

if (isTRUE(params$write_csv)) {
  readr::write_csv(
    joint_model_draws,
    gzfile(file.path(params$output_dir, "amis_joint_model_draws_direct_v2.csv.gz"))
  )
}

output_inventory <- tibble(
  file = list.files(params$output_dir, full.names = TRUE),
  size_mb = file.info(file)$size / 1024^2
) %>%
  arrange(desc(size_mb))

output_inventory

# Interpretation and limitations

This direct-bootstrap procedure estimates joint input uncertainty while conditioning on the
final survey calibration weights and external raking margins. It preserves the
observed within-respondent dependence and joint missingness structure of the
eight measures. It does not propagate uncertainty from constructing the raking
weights.

Respondents are resampled independently across state-period strata. The method
therefore does not impose temporal sampling correlation across the four
periods. This matches the repeated-cross-sectional interpretation of the AMIS
inputs but does not account for possible dependence caused by recurring
respondents or shared recruitment processes across survey years.

The joint bootstrap is used because it better represents the dependence
structure of the inputs, not because it is expected to produce narrower
intervals. Comparisons with the former independent-Beta approximation are
reported as methodological diagnostics.
